assertions.subject: Appendiceal neoplasms
assertions.quote: Neoplasms that occur in the appendix are predominantly gastroenteropancreatic neu-roendocrine tumors (or GEP-NETs, previously called carci-noids), mucinous neoplasms, or adenocarcinomas

assertions.subject: Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors (GEP-NETs or Carcinoid)
assertions.quote: Appendiceal carcinoid tumors are submucosal rubbery masses that are detected incidentally on the appendix

assertions.subject: Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors (GEP-NETs or Carcinoid)
assertions.quote: Carcinoid tumors of the appendix are relatively indolent but can develop nodal or hepatic metastases

assertions.subject: Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors (GEP-NETs or Carcinoid)
assertions.quote: Infrequently, these can be associ-ated with a carcinoid syndrome if there are hepatic metastases (2.9%)

assertions.subject: Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors (GEP-NETs or Carcinoid)
assertions.quote: For lesions that are less than 1 cm (95% of all lesions), a negative margin appendectomy is adequate
